description.narrative:
1. Two Trade Unions organizations managed de extension of the VCT@WORK initiative that allowed the provision of HIV/AIDS services for private sectors and union organizations reaching 193 workers.
2. The Indonesia Business and Disability Network was re-launched, and joint commitment was made between the Ministry of Manpower, the Employers Organization, and the Indonesia Business and Disability Network to promote the employment of people with disabilities. 1. The ILO provided technical and financial support to constituents in the extension of HIV/AIDS services. 193 workers were tested for HIV (177 males and 16 females) with 1 case reactive and referred to ARV treatment. In 2021, the extension of HIV service continued reaching additional private companies and trade unions by combining the regular HIV test and the innovative HIV self screening (in progress).
2. The ILO office facilitated the re-launched and the joint commitment, secretariat of the IBDN sits with the ILO Jakarta Office

description.narrative:
A review of national laws and policies vis-à-vis C190 was developed and, in June 2021, the report, including the recommendations concerning changes in laws and policies, was discussed and validated by tripartite constituents. Following this review, the Government along with employers¿f and workers¿f organisations have agreed to revise the Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) Guideline. This Guideline is considered a national policy guide for tripartite stakeholders. The revised EEO Guide is to be finalised by November 2021. It will be used for sensitization and training programs on how to prevent and protect from violence and harassment at the workplace scheduled for December 2021. These programs will target roughly 6,000 workers and employers.
Moreover, following the review of national laws and policies, tripartite constituents agreed on the following measures to be taken:
submitting the outcomes of regulatory analysis to the Government for further consideration and actions towards ratification;
undertaking a campaign on ratification of C190, and
developing a guideline and training module on addressing violence and harassment at work. The module will be developed by the ILO and UN WOMEN in collaboration with Ministry of Manpower and Ministry of Women Empowerment and Child Protection. The ILO provided technical support for the review of national laws and policies and for the organisation and delivery of the tripartite validation workshop. The ILO also facilitated the revision of the EEO Guide by hiring a national consultant to gather inputs and collect update activities related to violence and harassment, equality and non- discrimination from the tripartite constituents.
The ILO also supported the revision of the EEO and is planning to continue supporting the sensitization and training programs of roughly 6,000 target beneficiaries of workers and employers. These activities are planned by December 2021.
To further build on the momentum, the ILO is providing support to the tripartite constituents in their decision to organize a wide campaign for ratification of C 190. Finally, the ILO, along with UNWOMEN, is providing technical support to the Ministry of Manpower and Ministry of Women Empowerment and Child Protection for the development of a guide and training module on addressing violence and harassment at work. This guide and training module, which will be delivers in 2022, will target the tripartite constituents as well as the public at large.
